cleanIntro: SIG's field strip, from the only P365 revision that prints a P365-XMACRO parts diagram. The strip itself is the standard four-piece P365 procedure. What is XMACRO-specific is the slide: SIG's diagram shows the XMACRO with an integrated-compensator slide assembly and with a non-compensated slide assembly, and the cleaning changes depending on which one you own.

steps.title: Check what your XMACRO is actually fitted with
steps.action: Establish three things before you start: whether there is a manual safety lever on the frame, whether the grip module carries a magazine disconnect, and whether the front of your slide has an integrated compensator or is the plain non-compensated slide.
steps.prose: The magazine disconnect is not something to guess at on an XMACRO. SIG restricts the magazine-disconnect grip module to California compliant fire control units, and where it is fitted the trigger is mechanically blocked with the magazine out — which changes how the pistol behaves during clearing and during the function check at the end.
steps.aside: SIG's XMACRO parts diagram lists both an XMACRO slide assembly and a non-compensated slide assembly, so the compensator is a per-pistol question, not a model-wide one.
steps.quote: Magazine disconnect mechanisms are only available in California compliant FCU’s.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 18.7 P365 California Compliant Parts Diagram, p.122

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger clear of the trigger guard, press the magazine catch and let the XMACRO's magazine drop out of the grip module. Set it aside.
steps.prose: Unless yours is one of the California compliant fire control units, the pistol will still fire a round in the chamber with the magazine gone. Dropping the magazine removes the feed source, nothing more.
steps.quote: REMOVING THE MAGAZINE FROM THE FIREARM DOES NOT PREVENT A CHAMBERED ROUND FROM BEING FIRED UNLESS THE FIREARM IS EQUIPPED WITH A MAGAZINE DISCONNECT MECHANISM.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 9.5 Unloading and Clearing the Pistol, p.33
steps.warn: The magazine being out proves nothing about the chamber. That is the next step, and it is not optional.

steps.title: Lock the slide back and check the chamber twice
steps.action: Pull the slide fully rearward, push the slide catch lever up so it stays open, then look into the ejection port and down the magazine well and put a finger into both. Repeat the whole check.
steps.prose: SIG asks for two passes, visual and physical. On a compensated XMACRO the extra hardware at the muzzle end changes nothing about this — the chamber is still behind a short port and a case rim still reads as shadow.
steps.quote: Check the firearm twice, both visually and physically.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 9.5 Unloading and Clearing the Pistol, step 6, p.33

steps.title: Hold the slide open on the catch lever
steps.action: With the pistol cleared, draw the slide rearward again and push the slide catch lever up until the slide locks open on it. Ease forward until it stops hard against the lever.
steps.prose: This is the only position from which the takedown lever will rotate. If the lever feels frozen later, come back here first — a slide that has crept forward is the usual cause.
steps.quote: Lock the slide to the rear by pulling the slide rearward and pushing up on the slide catch lever.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.1 Field Strip the Pistol, step 2, p.50

steps.title: Rotate the takedown lever clockwise to its stop
steps.action: Rotate the takedown lever on the left of the frame clockwise about a quarter turn until it will go no further. Fingertip pressure is enough.
steps.prose: SIG scopes the tool exception in this step to the P365 SAS, whose lever is cut flush — not to the XMACRO. Your lever is a full one and turns by hand, so stiffness here means the slide is not fully locked back rather than that a screwdriver is called for.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever clockwise until it stops (P365 SAS requires a screwdriver or similar tool).
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.1 Field Strip the Pistol, step 3, p.50

steps.title: Release the catch with a hand on the slide
steps.action: Take a firm grip on the slide, pull it slightly rearward to unload the slide catch lever, let the lever drop, and keep control as the slide comes forward.
steps.prose: From this point the slide is held on by your hand alone. If your XMACRO has the compensated slide, do not use the compensator as a grip point — it is at the far end of a heavy assembly and gives you the worst possible leverage on it.
steps.caution: Eye protection from here on. The recoil spring assembly inside the slide is compressed.
steps.quote: Pull the slide slightly rearward to disengage the slide catch lever while maintaining control of the slide assembly.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.1 Field Strip the Pistol, step 4, p.52

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide assembly straight forward off the frame rails; the barrel and recoil spring come with it.
steps.prose: Straight forward and square. Lifting the rear as you pull binds the slide on the rails, and a bound slide gets forced, which is how rails get burred.
steps.quote: Pull the slide forward and off of the frame.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.1 Field Strip the Pistol, step 5, p.52

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down, push the recoil spring and guide forward toward the muzzle to unseat the guide head from under the barrel lug, then lift the rear of it up and away.
steps.prose: Forward first, then up — that is the order that frees the head. Reversing it traps the head against the lug and leaves you prying at a compressed spring inside a slide.
steps.caution: Keep the muzzle end pointed away from your face while the guide unseats.
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring and spring guide forward, then lift up and away from the slide to remove.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.1 Field Strip the Pistol, step 6, p.52

steps.title: Barrel out of the slide
steps.action: Push the barrel forward in the slide until the lug clears, then lift it out. It should lift free with no resistance.
steps.prose: Resistance means the recoil spring guide is still in the slide. Nothing here is press-fitted, so force is never the answer — go back and check what is still in place.
steps.quote: Slide the barrel forward and lift the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.1 Field Strip the Pistol, step 7, p.52

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide, barrel, recoil spring and guide assembly, frame and grip module. That is SIG's complete owner-level strip of an XMACRO.
steps.prose: The striker, the extractor and the fire control unit are all beyond what this manual authorises, and disassembly past this point voids the warranty. Note that SIG does not publish an owner procedure for removing an integrated compensator from an XMACRO slide — it is part of the slide assembly in the parts diagram, not a serviceable item.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly is sufficient to allow a thorough cleaning.
steps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.1 Field Strip the Pistol, note, p.53

deepSteps.title: Compensated slides only — nylon brush the comp and the slide front
deepSteps.action: If your XMACRO has the integrated-compensator slide, work a nylon brush through the compensator ports and across the front face of the slide until the caked residue is gone. If you have the non-compensated slide, skip this step entirely — there is nothing there to clean.
deepSteps.prose: A compensator sits directly in the gas path and cakes faster and harder than anything else on the pistol. SIG specifies nylon here, not bronze and not steel: the buildup is on finished external surfaces where a harder brush leaves marks. This is why the compensator question belongs in step 0 — the answer decides whether this step exists for you.
deepSteps.quote: If the slide has an integrated compensator, use a nylon brush to remove all residue buildup from the compensator and the front of the slide.
deepSteps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubrication, Slide Assembly, step 3, p.56

deepSteps.title: Check your floorplate type before you pry
deepSteps.action: Empty the magazine and look at the top of the floorplate for a tab. SIG's magazine note sorts the line by floorplate, so identify yours by looking rather than by the model name.
deepSteps.prose: This note is where an XMACRO owner can go wrong: SIG names XSERIES magazines, and standard P365 and SAS magazines, and does not name the P365-XMACRO in that sentence at all. The tab is what the punch has to press, so find out whether yours has one before you put a tool on it.
deepSteps.aside: SIG's optional-magazine section lists 17-round and 10-round XMACRO magazines; the 17-round is inside the size range the disassembly procedure below covers.
deepSteps.quote: Magazines for XSERIES models must have floor plates without tabs.
deepSteps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.4 Magazine Maintenance, note, p.64

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off — the insert is holding a compressed spring
deepSteps.action: Stand the empty magazine on the bench, press the insert tab inward through the floorplate hole with a punch, and slide the floorplate off while keeping a thumb over the insert.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is compressed the length of the tube and the insert is the only thing containing it. The tab needs to move just far enough to clear its notch — pressing hard and lifting the thumb together is what sends the insert across the room. SIG prints this procedure for the 10, 12, 15, 17, 21 and 25-round magazines.
deepSteps.aside: A 12-round extended magazine uses a floorplate retainer instead and takes a different first step.
deepSteps.quote: Using a punch or similar tool, push the tab of the magazine insert inward to release and remove the floorplate.
deepSteps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.4.1 Magazine Disassembly, step 1, p.65
deepSteps.warn: Eye protection. This is the one step in the guide where a part can leave under its own power.

deepSteps.title: Insert, spring and follower out of the tube
deepSteps.action: Ease the insert out of the bottom of the tube with the spring still on it, then draw spring and follower out behind. Note which way the follower faces before it clears.
deepSteps.prose: The follower is handed and will not feed inverted. Lay the parts out in removal order — the XMACRO's higher-capacity tube uses a long spring and it is easy to lose track of its ends.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the insert, magazine spring, and follower from the magazine tube.
deepSteps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.4.1 Magazine Disassembly, step 2, p.66

deepSteps.title: Scrub the tube and follower
deepSteps.action: Wipe the tube inside and out and the follower with a cloth, then run a soft brush wet with CLP down the tube and around the follower.
deepSteps.prose: Residue on the follower rails is what makes a high-capacity magazine drag on the last few rounds. Soft brush only — nothing steel goes inside a magazine tube.
deepSteps.quote: Wipe the magazine tube and follower with a cloth. Clean the magazine tube and follower with a soft brush and CLP.
deepSteps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.4.2 Magazine Cleaning, step 1, p.68

deepSteps.title: Light oil on the spring and tube exterior only
deepSteps.action: Light coat of CLP on the spring and on the outside of the tube, then wipe the inside dry.
deepSteps.prose: SIG oils the spring and the exterior, not the bore of the tube. Oil inside collects grit and transfers onto cartridges, and lubricated ammunition is its own problem.
deepSteps.quote: Apply a light coat of CLP to the spring and outside of magazine tube.
deepSteps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.4.2 Magazine Cleaning, step 3, p.68

deepSteps.title: Back together — floorplate on until the insert snaps
deepSteps.action: Fit follower and insert onto the spring, feed the follower into the tube and compress, then press the insert down and slide the floorplate on until the insert snaps into it.
deepSteps.prose: That snap is your only confirmation. Without it the floorplate is held by friction and will come off the first time the magazine lands on concrete.
deepSteps.quote: Press the insert and slide the floorplate onto the magazine tube until the insert snaps into the floorplate.
deepSteps.cite:
P365 
® PISTOLS — P/N 2700116-01 REV12 — 11.4.3 Magazine Assembly, step 3, p.70

cleaning.name: SLIDE ASSEMBLY
tasks: Strip all old lubricant before applying new
Cloth first, then a soft brush with CLP on heavy carbon
Extractor, rail slots and breech face free of dirt and residue
Light CLP in the frame rail slots of the slide
Striker channel stays dry — lubricant in it causes light strikes
Compensated slides: nylon brush through the comp and across the slide front (see Deep Clean)

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: CLP patch from the chamber end out past the muzzle, never from the muzzle back
Soak a few minutes to soften the carbon
Correct-caliber bronze brush on a rod, then dry patches until they come out clean
Feed ramp with a soft brush and CLP
Wipe the exterior with a CLP cloth; strip all oil from the bore before firing

cleaning.name: FRAME AND GRIP MODULE
tasks: Soft cloth over the frame and the XMACRO grip module
Cotton swabs into the corners; the frame rails get the attention
Light CLP on the frame rails and accessible moving parts
Wipe the magazine well clear of dust and residue

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING GUIDE ASSEMBLY
tasks: CLP and a soft brush, then a light coat back on
Do not disassemble it — SIG services it as a single unit
Replace at 2,500-round intervals; check for kinked coils or a loose head

reassembly: Confirm the barrel is clear, then drop it into the inverted slide.
Put the larger outer spring of the recoil spring guide assembly into the front of the slide and seat the guide head centred on the barrel lug.
Check the takedown lever is still rotated clockwise to its stop; the slide catch lever may need raising slightly before it will turn.
If your XMACRO has a manual safety, push the safety lever DOWN before the slide goes on — installing it with the lever up damages the pistol.

Run the slide onto the frame rails to the fully retracted position, lock it there on the slide catch lever, rotate the takedown lever counterclockwise to its stop, then press the catch lever down to release the slide.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber confirmed empty. Insert an empty magazine — audible click and it holds. Rack the slide fully back; the follower should push the slide catch lever up and lock the slide open. Press the magazine catch: the magazine must fall free under its own weight. If your XMACRO has a magazine disconnect, the striker must NOT release with the magazine out and must release with an empty magazine in. If it has a manual safety, the striker must NOT release with the safety engaged. Safety off: pull and hold the trigger for a loud click, hold it back and rack the slide, release for a light reset click, then pull again for a second loud click.
